question.text: What is a bonus issue of shares?

answer.text: Allotment of additional shares to existing shareholders without any payment
Issue of shares at a discounted price to the public
Issue of shares to employees at a preferential price
Issue of shares to institutional investors on preferential terms

explanation.text: The Logic: In a bonus issue, existing shareholders receive an allotment of additional shares without any consideration (payment). The company capitalizes its reserves to issue these free shares to existing investors. The Trap: Option (b) sounds similar but a bonus issue is free, not discounted. Option (c) describes a preferential or employee issue (shares issued to employees at a preferential price), not a bonus issue. Note: Bonus = free shares capitalized from reserves and allotted to existing shareholders. Rights = new shares offered to existing holders at a price.
